threads.body: Pending the discussion in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/19160#discussion_r3564889077, I think we should avoid process-local `-N` suffixes here. If no stable name exists, use a stable fallback and let duplicates merge so metric identities remain consistent across restarts.

I don't think this `getDbName()` fallback can ever fire. `ParseContext.build()` sets `dbNamespace` whenever it parsed a namespace or a database name, and the only two spots that set the `dbName` override (`MssqlUrlParser` and `JtdsUrlParser`) set the namespace in that same branch. Anything else comes back as `DbInfo.DEFAULT` with both null. Note also: `getDbName()` will be removed soon in 3.0.

```suggestion
    String dbNamespace = dbInfo.getDbNamespace();
```

The PR description still describes an earlier design that isn't what landed here: it talks about generated names like `c3p0-1`, keeping that generated name stable for the data source's lifetime, and removing the generated name state on unregister. This implementation instead derives `server.address:server.port/db.namespace` from the nested JDBC data source, falls back to the literal `c3p0`, and keeps no state at all. Could you update the Summary and Changes sections to match? The derived-endpoint approach is the one semconv actually recommends for an unnamed pool, so it's worth describing accurately.

Every other module that needs JDBC classes on the test agent depends on the jdbc javaagent module instead of a separately shaded jar (same thing @jaydeluca raised on the tomcat-jdbc one). That's also how the parser actually reaches this module in the released agent, so the test setup ends up closer to production. I tried this locally and all five tests here still pass.

```suggestion
  testInstrumentation(project(":instrumentation:jdbc:javaagent"))
```

The `compileOnly` shadow dependency above should stay as is — that's what gives you the parser signature with `DbInfo` relocated into the bootstrap package.
